title: Rollover of Expiring Commercial Natural Gas Supply Agreements to the Monthly Index Plan
content:
**Conversion at expiry.** When a Commercial Natural Gas Supply term reaches its contract end date without a renewal acceptance and without a pending cancellation, the agreement converts on the following day to the plan named as the rollover plan, with a term of 0 months, an empty contract end date, a plan change date set to the day after the expired contract end date, and a contract rate set to the rollover adder.

**Late or missing notices.** When either expiration notice was missing or not compliant, the expiring price is held first for the late-notice price hold, a number of billing cycles set in the plan schedule. During the hold the expiring price is recorded as the contract rate and billed as a fixed price; after the hold the contract rate becomes the rollover adder.

**No termination fee.** A rolled-over agreement carries no early termination fee.

## Input, judgement, outcome

| At the contract end date | Expiration notices | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Renewal accepted | Any | The conversion does not apply |
| Cancellation pending | Any | The conversion does not apply |
| Neither | Both issued and compliant | Converts the next day to the rollover plan at the rollover adder |
| Neither | Either missing or not compliant | Converts the next day to the rollover plan; the expiring price is held as a fixed price for the late-notice hold cycles, then the contract rate becomes the rollover adder |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Beacon Ridge Commercial Gas Fixed 12 agreement has a contract end date of 2025-12-31, both notices were compliant, and nothing was accepted or cancelled. On 2026-01-01 the agreement is on the rollover plan with a term of 0 months, no contract end date, a plan change date of 2026-01-01 and the rollover adder as its contract rate. From then on, ending the agreement carries no early termination fee.
